title: Hearty Sweet Corn and Bean Chowder
subtitle: with Cheesy Roasted Broccoli and Garlic Bread
description: Whether you're full-time vego or part-time only, our varied range of vegetarian dishes really hits the spot. Bursting with veggies, dairy, legumes, grains and nuts, they're packed with flavour, they’ll fill you up and they're totally mouth-watering too!

steps.text: Prep ingredients: Preheat the oven to 200C, fan-forced. Line an oven tray with baking paper. Cut the unpeeled potatoes into 1.5cm chunks. Cut the broccoli stem into 1cm chunks and cut the head into small florets. Thinly slice the spring onion. Finely chop or crush 1 garlic clove. Coarsely grate the cheese. Drain and rinse the corn and beans, keeping them separate.

Roast broccoli florets: Combine 2 tsp mayonnaise and 2 tsp water in a large bowl and season with salt and pepper. Add the broccoli florets, toss to coat and put on the lined tray. Roast for 10 mins or until tender and charred around the edges. Scatter the cheese over the broccoli florets and roast for a further 3 mins or until the cheese is melted.

Soften veggies: Meanwhile, put the country seasoning, 60ml (¼ cup) milk and 500ml (2 cups) boiling water in a heatproof jug and stir to dissolve. Heat 20g butter in a medium saucepan over medium heat. Cook the potato, broccoli stems, spring onion and garlic, stirring, for 4 mins. Add 1 tbs plain flour and cook, stirring, for 2 mins or until golden (see Kitchen 101).

Simmer chowder: Gradually add the milk mixture to the veggies, stirring constantly to prevent lumps forming. Add the corn and bring to the boil. Reduce the heat to medium and cook, stirring occasionally, for 8 mins or until the potato is tender. Add the beans and cook, stirring, for 2 mins or until warmed through. Remove the pan from the heat. Taste, then season with salt and pepper.

Bake bread and serve up: When the broccoli has finished cooking, remove from the oven and cover to keep warm. Increase the oven temperature to 220C. Put the garlic bread on an oven tray, butter-side up, and bake for 6 mins or until golden and crunchy. Divide the chowder among bowls and top with the cheesy broccoli. Serve with the garlic bread and enjoy!
Kitchen 101: It's important to cook the flour until it turns golden, so the finished chowder doesn't taste of raw flour.
